title: [Thrift] Limit depth of nested types using p_set_proto_depth
description:
Use a nested_type_depth preference to allow customization (default 25).

Fix incorrect display of 8 to 14 list & set lengths as negative values when displaying internal Thrift fields of compact PDU in sub-dissector.

Closes #17694

notes.body:
Done:

* The fix in the main case (no issue even with low `ulimit -S -s value`).
* An additional fix where short lengths were displayed as negative values due to the signedness of href (required for generic cases) seen in the same capture. [Can be split in another commit if preferred.]

Not done yet:

* Adaptation of specific sub-dissector to update `nested_type_depth` in case of failure to dissect (used when `fallback_on_generic` is set to `TRUE`).

Any remark would be appreciated.

@AndersBroman & @richvdh (& others) : I used 25 as the default depth for the moment, please take a look at your protocols to ensure this is enough for known real-life cases (it will still be configurable to a higher value but having a sane default is better).

Tests done with the Jaeger sub-dissector to override the limit at fallback and everything works as expected.

Fuzzing is ongoing but other than that, this MR is no longer a draft.
I couldn't merge this branch: Sorry, I can't merge requests marked as Work-In-Progress!

Nope, this is precisely the second issue I was talking about:

* `hf_num_item` holds the signed href (the generic element used when extended length is necessary).
* `hf_pos_item` holds the unsigned href (pos = positive, used when a single nibble can hold the length).

Using `hf_num_item` caused the length of 10 (0xa) to be displayed as -6, visible with the capture from #17694.
